findings.issue: connectionConfig test asserts cfg.mode === 'strict' (string literal) rather than ConnectionMode.Strict (enum value). The exposed object stores a raw string, while the VueFlow template prop binds the enum constant directly. The test correctly mirrors the exposed object, but a future refactor that aligns the object to use the enum would silently pass — the assertion does not prove the enum is what VueFlow receives.
findings.recommendation: After asserting cfg.mode === 'strict', add a companion assertion that ConnectionMode.Strict resolves to the same string: expect(ConnectionMode.Strict).toBe('strict'). This locks the contract between the object value and the enum, so a VueFlow upgrade that changes the enum's string value does not produce a silent mismatch.

findings.issue: The connectionConfig test verifies the exposed JS object but does not confirm that the VueFlow <VueFlow> component actually receives connection-mode and connection-radius as template props. The test validates the data path (JS object) but not the template binding path — a copy-paste error that binds the wrong variable in the template would not be caught.
findings.recommendation: This gap is acceptable to defer as noted in the spec (live pointer-drag is user-verified). If a snapshot or attribute-based DOM assertion is ever added, check that the rendered VueFlow root carries the expected attributes. No blocking action required.

summary: All five new tests are value-based and load-bearing. Litmus test passes for each: removing the core logic line (connectionConfig object, isValidConnection return, id='in' attribute, handleConnect resolution) causes each respective assertion to fail. The two new handleConnect tests with targetHandle='in' correctly prove the regression guard without weakening the existing targetHandle:null tests — both paths now have coverage. No existing connect/handle tests were weakened. Two minor findings: one notes a string-vs-enum assertion opportunity, one notes the template binding is not directly verified but is acceptably deferred per spec. Zero critical, zero major findings.
